rationale: CRANMOOD depression comparisons were inconclusive in healthy students given a cranberry drink. COMBAT confirms baseline PHQ-9 screening but has no reported randomized post-treatment depression comparison in the recovered reports and supplements. These studies leave the dried-cranberry hypothesis in Parkinson disease unresolved.

Standardized ginger powder gave an inconclusive anxiety comparison in healthy adults, and the SSRI adjunct abstract conflicts with itself about direction. The Parkinson extract trial has no posted results and the Parkinson formula ingredients remain unverified. Concentrated extracts produced favorable open-field results in rat neuropathy models. These comparisons leave fresh grated ginger and clinical Parkinson anxiety unresolved.
